name: Elishama
overview: Elishama was a male member of the tribe of Judah, uniquely identified as a son of David. His mention is brief, with no additional notes expanding on his life or role. His identity is primarily grounded in his lineage as part of the royal family of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Elishama means "G-d has heard" in Hebrew, reflecting a meaningful theophoric element. This proper name was not given directly by God but is recorded in Scripture, emphasizing divine attentiveness in its meaning.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Elishama as a son of David, situating him within the royal lineage. Beyond this, no other family relationships or descendants are noted in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Elishama's significance lies chiefly in his connection to King David, one of Israel's most pivotal figures. As a son of David from the tribe of Judah, he represents part of the royal heritage through which God's covenant promises were fulfilled. Although the biblical record provides limited detail about his personal contributions, his inclusion in the genealogy underscores the continuity of God's plan through David's descendants.
